title: Emergency stop and interlocks
summary: Make a running line stop when the emergency stop is pressed, show it with the red light and refuse to restart until Start is pressed again.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Stop every output while the emergency stop is pressed.
Remember the stop, so that releasing the button does not restart the line.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ThreeLevelLifts.st, add a Stopped memory: set it when EStopOk is FALSE, clear it only with Start, let it clear Active and light Red.
stages.checkpoint: Every output already depends on Active, so clearing Active stops the belts and the lifts together.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the stop: at 15.5 s the emergency stop is pressed while a lift may be moving; the line must stop, stay stopped when the button is released at 17 s, and run again only after the Start press at 17.5 s.
stages.checkpoint: Red on and every output off at 16 s; still stopped at 17.3 s; Red off and the line running again after Start.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter ignores the emergency stop, so the line keeps running; stop every output while EStopOk is FALSE, light Red, keep the stop remembered after the release and run the line again only with a new press of Start.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: In Tests, choose the saved zplc.json and run only the estop-interlocks scenario; watch the 3D view while it runs.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named estop-interlocks and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the stack light turn red and the belts and lifts stop when the scenario presses the emergency stop, and run again after Start.
stages.checkpoint: Red stays on after the release until Start, and the outputs fall in the same scan as EStopOk.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The AT assertions pin the stop at 16 s, the held stop at 17.3 s and the restart at 18 s; the interlocks that were already in the program are the same idea as in the 2.0 lesson interlock-guard-permissive.
stages.checkpoint: It does not establish a safety function: this is a stop written in the PLC program, not a safety-rated circuit, and it gives no stopping time, hardware timing, HIL, or certification. The grade cannot see a lift that drifts after the stop.

hints.text: Check EStopOk first: when it is FALSE set Stopped and clear Active; run the line again only in an ELSIF Start branch.
Light Red from Stopped; the outputs already depend on Active, so no output needs its own stop logic.

faultCases: The starter ignores the emergency stop, so the line keeps running; stop every output while EStopOk is FALSE, light Red, keep the stop remembered after the release and run the line again only with a new press of Start.
